about: The single source of the word lists the engine-side guards read. scripts/gen-agency-lexicon.mjs writes them into the JavaScript, Python and Go engines between BEGIN and END GENERATED GUARD LEXICON markers, and its --check (run by test/agency-lexicon.test.mjs) fails when any engine's copy drifts. Two guards read them. The negator window: a negator, or any n't contraction, among the two words before a match, with no clauseBreaks character between them. Strip keeps an intensifier there, and absolute.universal leaves an absolute there unmarked (its window also ends at a comma once a word stands between them). The imperative 'Never': a clause-initial 'never' followed by a lowercase word reads as advice and is not marked by absolute.universal, unless that word, after any neverPassThrough adverbs, is one of neverNonVerbs. The engines compare a word after ASCII-only lowercasing (a negator also after trimming apostrophes), so every word here is lowercase ASCII.
negatorsWhy: A word that negates the intensifier or absolute after it. Deleting 'extremely' from 'not extremely high' leaves 'not high', a stronger claim than the source made; 'not guaranteed' and 'hardly always' are disclaimers, not overclaims. Each must stand within two words of what it negates.
neverNonVerbsWhy: Words that, after a clause-initial 'never', open a fragment ('Never an issue.') or an inversion ('Never has a product been this good.'), both claims, and do not begin advice, so absolute.universal keeps 'Never' marked before them.
neverPassThroughWhy: Adverbs that may stand between 'Never' and its verb: the word after them decides. 'Never ever share it.' is advice; 'Never again will prices be this low.' is an inversion; 'Never again.' is a fragment.
neverAdviceOpenersWhy: Words that can begin advice after 'Never' as well as an inversion, so they are not neverNonVerbs: the advice stays unmarked and the claim goes unmarked with it. 'Never have regrets.' but 'Never have I seen...'; 'Never at any time disclose your PIN.' but 'Never in history has...'; 'Never so much as glance at it.'; 'Never should you share it.' The inversions are recorded misses, in the safe direction. The engines do not read this list; the tests and the differential probe each word as unmarked.
